item.description: China’s hybrid car exports to the European Union tripled in September from a year earlier, with shipments expected to remain elevated before an import cap agreed during recent trade talks takes effect. item.title: Michigan heckler the son of Republican adviser paid for ‘influencer marketing’ against El-Sayed
item.description: <p>Timmy Teepell’s firm paid $250,000 by America Next, which has been trying to gin up ‘organic’ opposition to El-Sayed</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/19/abdul-el-sayed-heckler-tommy">Man who heckled El-Sayed is former Josh Hawley aide, records show</a></p></li></ul><p>The man who attempted to ambush Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed with a question about his supposed allegiance to the Muslim Brotherhood – which El-Sayed parlayed into a viral clip for his campaign – is the son of a political operator who recently received $250,000 for “canvassing and influencer marketing” against El-Sayed, the Guardian has learned.</p><p>In the now-famous exchange, a man – first <a href="https://www.thehandbasket.co/p/tommy-teepell-abdul-el-sayed-viral-video-town-hall-josh-hawley">identified</a> by the Handbasket as Thomas “Tommy” Teepell – asked El-Sayed if he would “disavow” the Muslim Brotherhood. El-Sayed said he would, but then asked: “What are you implying? Do you assume that I wouldn’t?” What followed was a five-minute exchange that has <a href="https://x.com/electionsjoe/status/2112015325050892592">drawn</a> over 50 million views across several social media platforms, in which El-Sayed queries the man about the guarantees of religious freedom in the constitution.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/20/abdul-el-sayed-heckler">Continue reading...</a>

item.title: Ban on family visits to care homes at start of pandemic had ‘devastating consequences’, inquiry finds – UK politics live
item.description: <p>Heather Hallett, chair of the Covid inquiry, has just published the report from the inquiry’s module 6, looking at what happened in care homes</p><p><strong>Badenoch</strong> says Britain needs tax cuts.</p><p>We need to get out of the way of job creators who make our country richer. We need to encourage risk taking, wealth creation, enterprise.</p><p>Britain’s tax burden has never been higher. You are taxed on the heating in your home. You’re taxed at the petrol pump filling up your car. You’re taxed when you insure that car. You’re taxed if you take the family away on holiday. You’re taxed if you stay in the UK thanks to Andy Burnham’s tourist tax. You’re taxed to buy a home, taxed to live in a home, taxed to pass on your home. This is clearly not working. Britain does not feel better off.</p><p>Andy Burnham wrote in The Times yesterday about the moral outrage of the current benefit system. But as far as I could work out, his answer is to spend even more on benefits.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/politics/live/2026/oct/20/kemi-badenoch-john-healey-capital-gains-tax-budget-covid-inquiry-care-homes-uk-politics-latest-news">Continue reading...</a>

item.title: Downtown datacenter? AI plan floated for boarded-up San Francisco mall
item.description: <p>Developers propose turning San Francisco Centre into not a server-based facility but a ‘community-based AI exhibit’</p><p>Downtown San Francisco has shown signs of revival since being battered by the Covid pandemic, which led to what <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2023/may/28/san-francisco-vacant-buildings-housing-doom-loop">many called</a> a “doom loop” of vacant buildings, a worsening homelessness crisis, and dwindling public transit. But one highly visible reminder of the city’s struggle to recover remains: the San Francisco Centre mall, which sits at the heart of these urban renewal efforts and has been conspicuously <a href="https://abc7news.com/post/san-franciscans-say-goodbye-francisco-centre-permanently-shuts-doors/18460353/">boarded up</a> since January of this year.</p><p>A number of ideas have been floated for the mall’s reopening, including a multi-level <a href="https://sfstandard.com/2026/09/13/san-francisco-centre-mall-basketball/">sports complex</a>, <a href="https://therealdeal.com/san-francisco/2025/09/17/behemoth-san-francisco-centre-wont-see-daylight-as-housing/">housing</a>, and more traditional <a href="https://sfstandard.com/2026/07/08/san-francisco-centre-mall-falls-apart/">retail uses</a>. But now, another potential plan has emerged: the shuttered mall is being considered for an AI datacenter project, the San Francisco Chronicle <a href="https://www.sfchronicle.com/sf/article/downtown-mall-data-center-ai-22480545.php">reported</a>.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/20/san-francisco-mall-ai-datacenter">Continue reading...</a>
